front_blocks.md: Give four advantages of using a network.

back_blocks.md: Devices such as printers can be **shared**, reducing costs; **software licences** are cheaper than for individual computers; users can **share files and data**; there is access to **reliable central data**; files can be **backed up centrally**; users can **communicate**; and a network manager can **control access rights**.

front_blocks.md: Give four disadvantages of using a network.

front_blocks.md: Give three advantages of a WLAN.

back_blocks.md: Users can **connect anywhere in range of a WAP** without extra hardware or wiring, it can be used **indoors and out** so is highly flexible, and **additional access points** can be added easily to increase coverage.

front_blocks.md: Define **client-server network**.

back_blocks.md: It **hosts, delivers and manages** most of the resources and services to be consumed by the clients.

front_blocks.md: Define **network topology**.

front_blocks.md: How are devices connected in a bus topology?

back_blocks.md: All devices are connected by **one single 'bus' cable**, which is **terminated at each end**.

cards.front_md: How are devices connected in a bus topology?
cards.back_md: All devices are connected by **one single 'bus' cable**, which is **terminated at each end**.

front_blocks.md: What is the purpose of the terminators on a bus topology?

back_blocks.md: They **stop the signal bouncing back** and **causing errors**.

cards.front_md: What is the purpose of the terminators on a bus topology?
cards.back_md: They **stop the signal bouncing back** and **causing errors**.

front_blocks.md: How does a device on a bus topology decide whether to accept data?

back_blocks.md: Each device **'listens' to electrical signals**, **checks data packets for its specific address**, and **ignores packets it does not recognise**.

cards.front_md: How does a device on a bus topology decide whether to accept data?
cards.back_md: Each device **'listens' to electrical signals**, **checks data packets for its specific address**, and **ignores packets it does not recognise**.

front_blocks.md: Give three disadvantages of a bus topology.

back_blocks.md: **Low security**, since data is visible to all devices; **slow data transfer**, since it is prone to data collisions; and if the **cable breaks the whole network is affected**.

cards.front_md: Give three disadvantages of a bus topology.
cards.back_md: **Low security**, since data is visible to all devices; **slow data transfer**, since it is prone to data collisions; and if the **cable breaks the whole network is affected**.

front_blocks.md: Give two advantages of a bus topology.

back_blocks.md: It is **easy and cheap to set up**, since only one cable is needed, and it **does not rely on other network hardware** such as a central server or switch.

cards.front_md: Give two advantages of a bus topology.
cards.back_md: It is **easy and cheap to set up**, since only one cable is needed, and it **does not rely on other network hardware** such as a central server or switch.

front_blocks.md: How are devices connected in a star topology?

back_blocks.md: All devices connect to a **central switch**, which is an **intelligent device** that ensures traffic only goes to the intended device.

cards.front_md: How are devices connected in a star topology?
cards.back_md: All devices connect to a **central switch**, which is an **intelligent device** that ensures traffic only goes to the intended device.

front_blocks.md: How does traffic differ on a star topology using a hub rather than a switch?

back_blocks.md: A **hub sends traffic to all devices**, and each device accepts it only if the address matches; a **switch only sends traffic to the device** whose address matches.

cards.front_md: How does traffic differ on a star topology using a hub rather than a switch?
cards.back_md: A **hub sends traffic to all devices**, and each device accepts it only if the address matches; a **switch only sends traffic to the device** whose address matches.

front_blocks.md: Give two advantages of a star topology.

back_blocks.md: If **one cable fails the rest of the network still works**, a problem with **one device will not affect others**, and it is **more reliable** than a bus topology.

cards.front_md: Give two advantages of a star topology.

front_blocks.md: What is a full mesh topology?

back_blocks.md: A topology where **all computers are connected to all other computers**.

cards.front_md: What is a full mesh topology?
cards.back_md: A topology where **all computers are connected to all other computers**.

front_blocks.md: Name the two methods by which packets travel on a mesh topology.

back_blocks.md: **Routing**, where devices are given routing logic to send packets by the shortest route, and **flooding**, where all packets are sent to all devices with no routing logic.

cards.front_md: Name the two methods by which packets travel on a mesh topology.
cards.back_md: **Routing**, where devices are given routing logic to send packets by the shortest route, and **flooding**, where all packets are sent to all devices with no routing logic.

front_blocks.md: Give two advantages of a mesh topology.

back_blocks.md: If **one cable fails the network still works** because data can use an **alternate route**, it provides **high fault tolerance** through multiple paths, and it is **very reliable** for critical systems.

cards.front_md: Give two advantages of a mesh topology.
cards.back_md: If **one cable fails the network still works** because data can use an **alternate route**, it provides **high fault tolerance** through multiple paths, and it is **very reliable** for critical systems.

front_blocks.md: Give three disadvantages of a mesh topology.

back_blocks.md: It requires **lots of hardware, cables and switches**, has a **high cost to set up**, and is **hard to scale** because adding new devices is complex.

cards.front_md: Give three disadvantages of a mesh topology.
cards.back_md: It requires **lots of hardware, cables and switches**, has a **high cost to set up**, and is **hard to scale** because adding new devices is complex.

back_blocks.md: **Accessibility** from anywhere with an internet connection, easy **sharing and collaboration**, **scalability** as storage can be increased or decreased, **reliability** since data is backed up across multiple servers, **security features** such as encryption and multi-factor authentication, no need to **buy expensive storage hardware**, no need to **hire specialist IT staff**, and it is **eco-friendly**.

cards.front_md: Who owns and manages the servers in a public cloud, compared with a private cloud?

cards.front_md: How does access differ between a public and a private cloud?

front_blocks.md: Define **subnetting**.

back_blocks.md: Subnetting is the process of **dividing a larger network into smaller, more manageable parts** called **subnets**, each working like a mini-network within the main network.

front_blocks.md: Give three benefits of subnetting.

back_blocks.md: It **reduces network traffic**, **improves speed and performance** by keeping data in its local subnet, **increases security** by limiting access, is **easier to manage and maintain**, and **improves organisation** by grouping devices by department or function.

front_blocks.md: What kind of network is subnetting commonly used in?

front_blocks.md: Define **dynamic IP address**.

back_blocks.md: A dynamic IP address is **temporarily assigned when a device connects to the network**, taken from a **pool of available IP addresses**.

front_blocks.md: Define **URL**.

front_blocks.md: Define **Domain Name System (DNS)**.

back_blocks.md: The DNS **translates domain names into IP addresses**, so users do not have to remember the IP address of every website they visit.

front_blocks.md: What does a browser check before contacting a DNS server?

front_blocks.md: What happens if a DNS server cannot find the IP address for a domain?

front_blocks.md: What does a root server do in DNS resolution?

back_blocks.md: It **points to the correct Top-Level Domain (TLD) server**, which in turn points to the **authoritative DNS server** for that domain.

front_blocks.md: What does the authoritative DNS server do?

front_blocks.md: Define **DNS propagation**.

back_blocks.md: DNS propagation is the **updating of the DNS** when a domain is registered or its server IP address changes, which **may take some time to spread across the internet**.
